Kiran Kedlaya and Lenny Ng 

A-1 Yes, it does follow. Let P be any point in the plane. Let ABCD be any square with center P. Let E,F,G,H be the midpoints of the segments $AB,BC,CD,DA$ , respectively. The function  must satisfy the equations

If we add the last four equations, then subtract the first equation and twice the second equation, we obtain $0=$ $4f{\left(P\right)}$ , whence $f(P)=0$ 

Remark. Problem 1 of the 1996 Romanian IMO team selection exam asks the same question with squares replaced by regular polygons of any (fixed) number of vertices.

$$\ln(f(x))=\frac{-2\ln\cos(6x+\pi/4)+\ln\sin(6x+\pi/4)}{6}+c,$$

$2^{-1/12}\left(\frac{\sin(6x+\pi/4)}{\cos^{2}(6x+\pi/4)}\right)^{1/6}$ 



Remark. The answer can be put in alternate forms using trigonometric identities. One particularly simple one is
